description: We are a team of three Computer Science students passionate about turning NASA Earth observation data into practical, AI-driven tools for sustainable agriculture. For the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge, we are building an intelligent decision-support platform that combines real-time NASA agroclimatology and soil moisture datasets with machine learning to help farmers optimize crop rotations, improve soil health, and build resilience against changing weather patterns.
summary:
Field Shift is a web-based farm decision support tool that enables farmers to explore how to adapt crop-rotation strategies to new conditions. NASA Earth observation data are provided that are NASA POWER (precipitation, temperature and root-zone soil wetness), active and live for all land locations, and MODIS NDVI satellite vegetation data for our demo field in Ames, IOWA, USA. These time series are converted to five drought-related stress indicators, drought risk, heat stress, rainfall variability, soil moisture decline and crop greenness decline and four crop rotations are then compared to the five with the farmer's priorities in mind which are saving water, improving soil moisture, maximizing yield.

In response to this challenge, NASA is providing integrated management of climate and weather data with crop characteristics and farmers' preferences to allow farmers to consider rotational models to improve soil health and to adapt to changing temperatures, rainfall and water deficits. All recommendations include clear reasons, and hotter, drier what-ifs are included with the sliders. It is important as farmers seek clarity, transparency and data-driven advice to safeguard soil, conserve water and ensure long-term resilience in the face of increasing climate pressures.
details:
Field Shift is a web application to suggest crop rotation strategies for a selected site. After user selects a location through the click of the map or a pre-set location, the user is provided with the daily NASA POWER data (rainfall, max temp, soil wetness of root zone, 2019-2023) for that exact location. It also requires MODIS MOD13Q1 satellite vegetation data (250 m, 16-day) of the Earth's surface, gathered by NASA AppEEARS, for our demo field in Ames, Iowa. These raw time series are transformed to five 0-100% indicators of drought risk, heat stress, rainfall variability, soil moisture declines, and the decline of greenness in crops. The four possible rotations are scored with each other for resilience, soil health and yield, and the farmer's priority (save water, improve soil, maximize yield or custom weights), and these scores are aggregated. All results include simple statements explaining the why. What-if sliders enable an additional application of drought or heat to help test a more extreme future, and a Compare tab allows for a side-by-side display of two rotations.

Benefits

Field Shift provides farmers clarity and prioritized advice. No black box, every rotation ranking has clear explanations in simple terms and the result is influenced by the farmer's objectives (save water, improve soil, maximize yield, etc. or custom weights). It can be applied to any land location, uses NASA POWER data that is global, requires no training data or yield information, and is entirely based on free, open data from NASA. It's also easy to operate and use, and a farmer or adviser can get a solid suggestion in a matter of seconds

Impact

The expected outcome is that this will enable farmers and agricultural advisers to select the most appropriate rotation, which will minimize risks to soil, water and crop yields due to changing rainfall and temperatures. Field Shift helps equip farmers with the knowledge and tools to act on NASA Earth observations, promoting a more resilient future for their farms. The data pipe will run anywhere in the world and once the data is localized in other parts of the world, the tool can be scaled there.

Tools Used

  • Language: Python
  • Libraries: Streamlit, pandas, requests, Plotly, Folium (streamlit-folium), reverse_geocoder, pycountry
  • Data: NASA POWER API; MODIS MOD13Q1 via NASA AppEEARS and Earthdata
  • Development: VS Code, Git and GitHub
  • Hardware: standard laptops, no special equipment
  • AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) was used to help write and debug code.

Project Creativity

Field Shift translates raw satellite and climate information into actionable and prioritised advice, rather than a generic map or forecast. With what-if drought and heat sliders, farmers can try other scenarios to explore harsher futures. Click anywhere on the map to grab real-time NASA data that point. Resilient and healthy soils will yield with a side-by-side comparison view, which also allows for custom locations to be read through an offline place-name lookup.

Factors
We thought about data availability: climate data is available all over the world, but vegetation data was collected from satellites, which required manual export and so is loaded into our demo field in Ames, Iowa. Instead of predicting the outcome of the rotation, we opted for explainability, and created a transparent rule-based scoring model, as we cannot get rotation outcome data to train on. We acknowledged limitations: The rotation traits are estimates based on the agronomic environment and optimized for Iowa, and NASA POWER is a coarse-resolution, gridded product. We also ported the build to be a neat, reliable prototype that had cached data to make reliable demos. Future plans involve the development of localized crop libraries, NDVI for any point via the AppEEARS API, further, NASA datasets like SMAP and ECOSTRESS, and validation with actual crop yield data.
